nodes.label: QAC Wards Accreditation System
nodes.rationale: Accreditation workflow system for the PUP Quality Assurance Center: a public information site plus role-gated internal portals, single Next.js app, single domain.

nodes.label: Accreditation Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: document submission -> internal review -> accreditor visit -> status publication, with an audit trail behind it.

nodes.label: Document UUID Stamping
nodes.rationale: Every uploaded PDF carries a UUID written into the file itself, so document integrity survives outside the database.
nodes.community_name: Shared URL vs Role-Prefixed URL Rule

nodes.label: Audit Log of State Transitions
nodes.rationale: Accreditation state transitions are recorded in Postgres for auditability.

nodes.label: No Public Self-Registration
nodes.rationale: Accounts are provisioned by QAC Admin; public sign-up is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: Single App, Single Domain
nodes.rationale: One Next.js app serves both the public site and all internal portals; public and internal are split by route, not by deployment.

nodes.label: Workflow State Persisted in Postgres
nodes.rationale: XState owns transition and guard logic only; the actual state lives in Postgres so it is queryable and auditable.

nodes.label: Access Control Enforced at the Database
nodes.rationale: Supabase RLS, not only middleware. A portal route being reachable must never be the only thing standing between a role and another role's data.
nodes.norm_label: access control enforced at the database

nodes.label: Open Questions Blocking Phases 3+
nodes.rationale: Per-role permission matrix, the accreditation state machine, the data model, account provisioning, email triggers, and audit-log retention are all unspecified.
nodes.community_name: Can One Person Hold Two Roles?

nodes.label: Design System Rule - tokens only
nodes.rationale: All colors, fonts and type sizes must come from design/figma-tokens.md; never invent hex values, font families or px sizes outside that file, because it mirrors the client's existing Figma prototype.

nodes.label: Component Kit Rule
nodes.rationale: If a piece of UI appears on more than one screen it is a component: put it in the kit, never copy-paste into a second page. A kit component owns its own look; pages pass data and variants, not styling.

nodes.label: Kit Components Are Presentational
nodes.rationale: Kit components take fake data via props so the swap to real data is a page-level change.

nodes.label: Literal /portal Segment, Not a Route Group
nodes.rationale: Route groups contribute nothing to the URL, so (portal)/accreditations collides with the public /accreditations and the dev server 500s. The literal segment also buys a fail-closed matcher ["/portal/:path*"].
nodes.norm_label: literal /portal segment, not a route group

nodes.label: Never Run Git
nodes.rationale: The project owner runs git add/commit/push themselves; the agent prints the command as one copy-pasteable block instead.

nodes.label: Commit Message Rules
nodes.rationale: Simple, plain, one line. No conventional-commit prefixes, no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with trailer, no multi-line body unless asked.

nodes.label: pnpm allowBuilds (sharp, unrs-resolver)
nodes.rationale: Native postinstall builds explicitly allowed for sharp and unrs-resolver.

nodes.label: Font Family Tokens
nodes.rationale: Inter body, Playfair Display SC for the PUP wordmark, Poppins for QAC, Inria Serif footer, Roboto Serif for the accreditation-status heading.

nodes.label: Derived Tokens - pending client sign-off
nodes.rationale: Five colors and four sizes cannot dress a portal, so surface, positive, alert, holiday, 10px/9px steps and two shadows were measured off the portal frame exports. Real measured values, not inventions, but unconfirmed by the client. This section is the only sanctioned place for a value outside the token list.

nodes.label: The 31px Heading Snap
nodes.rationale: Both the dashboard banner and the login hero measure 31px, for which there is no token, so both ship at --text-title 36px. Costs 1.52% whole-screen diff versus 1.19% at 31px. If adopted exactly, 31px should become a token rather than an arbitrary value on two screens.

nodes.label: Login Copyright Below the Token Floor
nodes.rationale: The copyright line measures ~7.5px; --text-micro at 9px is the smallest token, so it ships ~20% wider than the prototype. No token can serve it exactly.
nodes.norm_label: login copyright below the token floor

nodes.label: Token Snap Rule
nodes.rationale: Snap to the nearest token when one exists, use an arbitrary value only when none can serve, and flag it. The prototypes use more sizes than the four the token file defines.

nodes.label: Cap-Height Font-Size Recovery
nodes.rationale: font-size ~= capHeight / 0.727 for Inter. Ink runs vary with which glyphs a line contains; the cap height of one flat-topped letter (T, F, H, M) is stable.

nodes.label: Cap-Top to CSS Margin Formula
nodes.rationale: capTop = boxTop + (lineHeight - 1.21*fontSize)/2 + 0.242*fontSize. Predicted every About margin to within ~10px on the first try.

nodes.label: Screenshot Stitching Method
nodes.rationale: Brute-force row-match each overlapping capture pair over the FULL range; a truncated search window silently locks onto a bogus match in a blank region. Reject err-0 matches whose band is uniform.

nodes.label: Do Not Infer Absent Content From a Gap
nodes.rationale: On About, a plausible bottom padding closed the gap after the chiefs - two whole staff rows were hiding in there. Ask for the missing screenshot instead.
nodes.norm_label: do not infer absent content from a gap

nodes.label: Image Cache Holds Only the Latest Message
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude/image-cache/<session-id>/ is renumbered each time, so measure every batch the moment it lands. Eyeballing a render is good to about +/-10px, not enough for margin work.
nodes.norm_label: image cache holds only the latest message

nodes.label: Express Crops as Viewport-Width Ratios
nodes.rationale: The client's browser is ~1849px wide and test viewports are 1440, so absolute px crops do not transfer. aspect-[w/h] + object-cover + a percentage object-position is scale-invariant.

nodes.label: portal-scale Zoom Utility
nodes.rationale: The portal is measured in literal px off a 1440x810 frame, so on a wider window it holds absolute size and shrinks proportionally. portal-scale zooms it by clamp(1, tan(atan2(100vw,1440px)) * 0.9, 2). The @property registration is load-bearing: it computes on :root where zoom is still 1, instead of feeding back on itself.

nodes.label: The *0.9 Damping Is Deliberate
nodes.rationale: A strict frame-width scale read a touch large to the owner (2026-07-23), so it is damped 10%. It is the tuning knob. Side effect: nothing scales until ~1600 wide, since below that the damped ratio is under the floor of 1.

nodes.label: zoom Does Not Rescale Viewport Units
nodes.rationale: A plain h-screen on the zoomed element lays out scale-times too tall (360px of overflow at 1920) and steals scrolling from main. The utility owns height: calc(100dvh / var(--portal-scale)) for exactly that reason.
nodes.norm_label: zoom does not rescale viewport units

nodes.label: text-title 1.5 Line-Height Trap
nodes.rationale: Tailwind v4 gives text-title a 1.5 line-height (54px) where the prototypes use ~1.2. Every heading needs explicit leading-[1.2] or the page drifts ~11px per heading - the biggest single source of vertical error on About.

nodes.label: Next <Image> True Pixel Size Rule
nodes.rationale: width/height must be the file's TRUE pixel size or artifacts bake into the cached WebP. After changing a file in public/, rm -rf .next/dev/cache/images.

nodes.label: JSX Silently Eats Spaces Around
nodes.rationale: Guard with a DOM assertion comparing textContent to the expected string; putting copy in string arrays sidesteps it entirely.

nodes.label: Ink Overflow Needs scrollWidth, Not getBoundingClientRect
nodes.norm_label: ink overflow needs scrollwidth, not getboundingclientrect

nodes.label: Lazy Images Are Blank in a fullPage Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Scroll first, then waitForFunction over document.images checking complete && naturalWidth > 0.
nodes.norm_label: lazy images are blank in a fullpage screenshot

nodes.label: Next Dev Indicator Corrupts Pixel Scans
nodes.norm_label: next dev indicator corrupts pixel scans

nodes.label: About Page Match Facts
nodes.rationale: max-w-[1152px] container, hero cropped to the prototype band ratio, the only justified text on the site, employee PNGs ship with a 5px frame baked into the file, and the prototype's oversized PALMA/DISTOR names were normalised on purpose.

nodes.label: Accreditations Page Match Facts
nodes.rationale: Hero aspect-[3.66] object-[center_38%] is settled - a tighter crop was tried and rejected. Stat cards 168x168, 61px gap, numeral gold keyline is four 1px offset text-shadows.

nodes.label: Gov. Recognitions Page Match Facts
nodes.rationale: Content is placeholder matching the prototype; the RECOGNITIONS array is the swap point. The hero is soft in the source asset - needs a client re-export >=1850px, not a quality flag.

nodes.label: Campuses Page Match Facts
nodes.rationale: Route is /about/campuses. The card grid is flex-wrap + justify-center, not grid, which is what centres the lone 22nd card that grid-cols-3 would left-align.

nodes.label: Campuses Stat Band Scaled Up on Request
nodes.rationale: The client asked for the band bigger than the prototype (2026-07-22), so it is deliberately off-prototype. The 365px side rules could not survive the scale-up and are now flex-1; do not restore w-[365px] without shrinking the type back.
nodes.norm_label: campuses stat band scaled up on request

nodes.label: About Dropdown Measured Spec
nodes.rationale: Matched to within 1px. bg-gray/15 over white computes to exactly #EBEBEB, the measured fill, so no arbitrary hex was needed. The prototype shows no active-page styling on dropdown items, so that distinction was deliberately removed rather than overlooked.

nodes.label: Client Rejected the Hover Pill
nodes.rationale: Hover must darken the font only, no container background. The active link keeps its solid maroon pill - that is the current-page indicator, not hover.

nodes.label: Navbar Height Mismatch: 58px vs 80px
nodes.rationale: The prototype navbar is ~58px tall against our 80px and its wordmark is all-caps. Not reconciled, and touching it moves every page.

nodes.label: Missing Employee Portrait Assets
nodes.rationale: PALMA, ENTIENZA, DISTOR and TRANCE were lifted 1:1 from client screenshots and re-framed; swap when real exports arrive.

nodes.label: Prototype Content Slips Reproduced Faithfully
nodes.rationale: Two reds on the campuses stat band (#990000 vs the #800000 token), ALFONSO and CABIAO both citing RA 11754, and inconsistent statute emphasis were reproduced rather than normalised, and flagged to the client instead.

nodes.label: UI-First Phase Reorder (2026-07-23)
nodes.rationale: All portal UI is built static from the Figma (3a) before any auth or database wiring (3b). Second reason: the client's database and full system flow are still unknown, so schema and RLS written now would be guesswork - and RLS is the most expensive thing to redo, since policies touch every table and every per-role test. Screens are cheaper to rebuild than policies.

nodes.label: The Figma Export Is the Only Blocker Left in 3a
nodes.rationale: The owner has Figma access to every role's frames; several folders are still empty awaiting a drop. DesignSync is not a Figma bridge, so frames cannot be pulled programmatically.
nodes.norm_label: the figma export is the only blocker left in 3a
nodes.community_name: The Figma Export Is the Only Blocker Left in 3a

nodes.label: Figma Frames Are 1440x810 at 2x
nodes.rationale: Settled 2026-07-23 and recorded in assets/FIGMA/README.md; halve every measurement taken off a PNG.

nodes.label: Phases 1-2 Are Done But Not Frozen
nodes.rationale: Token gaps, asset re-exports and the prototype navbar reconciliation can all send signed-off public pages back for rework.
nodes.norm_label: phases 1-2 are done but not frozen

nodes.label: Navbar Spec
nodes.rationale: Logo lockup left with the PUP line in Playfair Display SC and the QAC line in Poppins, nav links Home / About (dropdown) / Gov. Recognitions / Accreditations, circular account icon right. Active link is a maroon pill with white text.

nodes.label: GOVPH Footer Spec
nodes.rationale: Maroon background, four columns - Republika seal and public-domain notice, About GOVPH, Government Links, QAC contact block - with a centered copyright bottom bar. Static, identical for public and portal pages.

nodes.label: npm Was Used, Not pnpm
nodes.rationale: The plan originally said pnpm but the build ran on npm; package-lock.json is the lockfile in the repo. PRD.md still lists pnpm as the package manager.

nodes.label: Per-Page Build Loop Protocol
nodes.rationale: Build one page, screenshot it live via browser automation, show the project owner, wait for confirm or adjust, then move on. Never batch several pages and screenshot at the end.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Done But Not Frozen
nodes.rationale: Token gaps, deliberate departures, placeholder content, missing assets and the navbar reconciliation are all still open and can each send a page back for rework.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Shipped Flat Routes
nodes.rationale: The (public)/(portal) route groups are not set up; do that as one migration when auth lands, not piecemeal.

nodes.label: No-Hardcoded-Values Criterion Only Partially Met
nodes.rationale: The About cream band and arbitrary type sizes the token scale cannot express are carried deliberately, each isolated in a named constant with a comment. The token file needs the client's missing values before this closes cleanly.

nodes.label: Phase 3b - Auth + Role Gate
nodes.rationale: Not the current phase. Its per-role page inventory blocker no longer exists; everything else - the literal /portal segment, the fail-closed matcher, RLS, the next= guard, the (public) migration - still applies.

nodes.label: (portal) Route Group URL Collision
nodes.rationale: Verified against this repo 2026-07-22, not assumed. Parenthesised segments scope layouts but contribute nothing to the URL, so a probe at (portal)/accreditations/page.tsx fails the dev server with HTTP 500: 'You cannot have two parallel pages that resolve to the same path.' /accreditations, /calendar and /campuses are all names both sides want.

nodes.label: Decision: a Literal /portal Segment
nodes.rationale: (public) stays a route group because it only needs a shared layout; portal is a literal segment because it needs a shared namespace.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Middleware Matcher
nodes.rationale: matcher: ["/portal/:path*"] is one rule, fail-closed - any route added under /portal is protected the moment the file exists. Enumerating bare paths fails open: the day someone adds /reports and forgets the matcher entry, that page is public.

nodes.label: RLS Is the Authorization Boundary
nodes.rationale: Middleware only redirects unauthenticated visitors; it cannot answer whether this representative may read program 999. A user requesting a record they do not own must get zero rows from RLS and a 404, never a middleware pass over a populated page.

nodes.label: A Service-Role Query Is a Full RLS Bypass
nodes.rationale: Server Components and Route Handlers must query through the user's session client, not the service-role key.
nodes.norm_label: a service-role query is a full rls bypass

nodes.label: Role Claim Belongs in app_metadata
nodes.rationale: Never user_metadata, which users can edit themselves - that is a privilege-escalation path.

nodes.label: next= Open-Redirect Guard
nodes.rationale: Deep links survive auth via ?next=, defaulting to /portal, but next must be validated as a relative path beginning with /portal or it is an open redirect.

nodes.label: /portal Is the Role Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: No separate /portal/dashboard; /portal itself dispatches on the role claim.
nodes.community_name: Can One Person Hold Two Roles?

nodes.label: Shared URL vs Role-Prefixed URL Rule
nodes.rationale: If two roles can open the same database row it gets one URL and the role decides what renders; a feature for exactly one role gets a role-prefixed URL. Two stack-specific reasons to resist role-prefixed URLs for shared records: nodemailer notifications would have to resolve the recipient's role to build a link, and pdf-lib document UUIDs need a stable resolution target.
nodes.norm_label: shared url vs role-prefixed url rule
nodes.community_name: Shared URL vs Role-Prefixed URL Rule

nodes.label: Per-Role Views Are a Rendering Split, Not a Routing Split
nodes.rationale: 'Different pages per role' most often means different views and actions over shared objects. Only split the route when the underlying data is genuinely disjoint.
nodes.norm_label: per-role views are a rendering split, not a routing split
nodes.community_name: Shared URL vs Role-Prefixed URL Rule

nodes.label: Do Not Encode Workflow State in the Path
nodes.rationale: /portal/accreditations/[id]/pending-review rots the moment the record transitions. Keep the bare id and render from the state persisted in Postgres.
nodes.norm_label: do not encode workflow state in the path

nodes.label: (public) Route Migration
nodes.rationale: One atomic change: move the flat public routes into (public)/, move Navbar + Footer out of the root layout, leave login/ where it is, and confirm every public URL is byte-identical afterwards.

nodes.label: Can One Person Hold Two Roles?
nodes.rationale: If yes, the role dispatcher needs a role switcher and role-prefixed URLs become actively harmful. Also changes whether role is a column or a join table, and every RLS policy after it.
nodes.norm_label: can one person hold two roles?
nodes.community_name: Can One Person Hold Two Roles?

nodes.label: Phase 3a - Portal UI (static, no backend)
nodes.rationale: Build every screen of all four internal roles as static UI matching the owner's Figma. When the backend lands, the screens should not change - only their data source.

nodes.label: assets/FIGMA/ Is the Only Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: One folder per role plus _shared/, login/ and register/, numbered in build order. If a folder is empty the owner has not exported it yet - ask, do not invent the screens.
nodes.norm_label: assets/figma/ is the only source of truth
nodes.community_name: The Figma Export Is the Only Blocker Left in 3a

nodes.label: The Vocabulary-Mismatch Blocker
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 sat blocked for two sessions on a per-role page inventory that was never missing: the owner had the full Figma the whole time. The vocabulary ('inventory', 'shell', 'component kit') stopped them recognising what was being asked for. Ask in plain words, and confirm a block is real before declaring it.

nodes.label: Sanction for Deriving Missing Portal Colors
nodes.rationale: Five colors and four type sizes cannot dress a portal - no status-badge colors, no border, hover or disabled, and a large gap between 15px body and 36px title. Derive from maroon/yellow/gray and record every addition in figma-tokens.md under 'derived, pending client sign-off'. That section is the only sanctioned place.
nodes.norm_label: sanction for deriving missing portal colors

nodes.label: Dev-Only Role Switcher
nodes.rationale: So all four roles are clickable without real accounts. Must be trivially removable - it is a preview affordance, never an auth mechanism.

nodes.label: Role Slug Is program_representative
nodes.rationale: Owner chose it over academic_representative on 2026-07-23.

nodes.label: Backend Explicitly Out of Scope for 3a
nodes.rationale: No Supabase client, middleware, RLS, API routes, sessions, email or PDF processing. Nothing @supabase/* is installed and no .env* exists - keep it that way. The (public) migration is also not part of this phase.
nodes.norm_label: backend explicitly out of scope for 3a

nodes.label: Fake Data Typed Into the Files
nodes.rationale: Kept in a clearly-named array per screen so the swap point is obvious when the backend arrives.
nodes.norm_label: fake data typed into the files

nodes.label: Phase 3a UI Build Runbook
nodes.rationale: The procedure to 03a's policy: the per-screen loop, measurement rules, the verify setup, kit discipline, the identity seam, and the traps that have already cost time.

nodes.label: Per-Screen Build Loop
nodes.rationale: Build one screen, screenshot it live, diff it, show the owner, wait for confirm. It was overridden by the owner for frames 02-06, which measurably cost accuracy versus the dashboard's per-screen loop. Concession that works: build the first screen of a new role alone to establish that role's geometry family, then batch within the role.

nodes.label: Exports Are 2x of 1440x810 - Halve Everything
nodes.rationale: Halving lands the QAC wordmark on exactly 20px, nav labels 15, stat numerals 20, LEVEL n 12 and the top bar 59 - which is what settled the question.

nodes.label: Playwright Verify Setup
nodes.rationale: Viewport 1440x810 with deviceScaleFactor 2 gives a 2880x1620 PNG identical in size to the export, so landmarks compare as raw integers. Never measure a portal screen wider than 1440 - the shell zooms above that and every landmark will be wrong.

nodes.label: The 2.8% Antialiasing Pixel-Diff Floor
nodes.rationale: Resize both to 2880x1620 and count pixels differing >30/255. ~2.8% is the antialiasing-only floor; 4% is fine; 9%+ means something structural, or artwork that differs from what the designer used.

nodes.label: Content Padding Differs Per Screen Family
nodes.rationale: Dashboard/assignment/events/reports 57px, document browser 74px, profile 81px. Measure it per family; do not assume.
nodes.norm_label: content padding differs per screen family

nodes.label: The Identity Seam
nodes.rationale: The signed-in user is a hardcoded constant, so no other role is reachable without editing source. Replace it with getCurrentUser() reading a dev cookie into PORTAL_USERS. The cookie holds a user key, not a role, because the top bar shows name, position and avatar - switching role alone would leave one person's name on every role. Later this becomes supabase.auth.getUser() + app_metadata.role: one function body changes.

nodes.label: The Sidebar Must Receive the User
nodes.rationale: PortalTopBar and PortalSidebar both import the hardcoded constant directly today. The sidebar is a client component because it needs usePathname, so it has to receive the user as a prop rather than call the server-only accessor.
nodes.norm_label: the sidebar must receive the user

nodes.label: An Empty Sidebar Is by Design, Say So
nodes.rationale: PORTAL_NAV only defines qac_personnel. Until a role's frames land its sidebar is empty by design - say so in the switcher rather than rendering a blank rail, or it reads as a bug.
nodes.norm_label: an empty sidebar is by design, say so

nodes.label: Kit Discipline
nodes.rationale: Read kit/index.ts before building any screen. Reuse what is there, extend with a prop rather than forking a near-duplicate, and the moment a second screen needs something a page has inline, move it to the kit and update the first screen.

nodes.label: Keep Formatting in Components, Not Fake Data
nodes.rationale: Stat.note is currently a finished sentence ('1.10% Since last month'); it should take deltaPct and compose in StatCard. This is what makes the eventual real-data swap a data change instead of a rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: keep formatting in components, not fake data

nodes.label: data.ts Is the Single Backend Swap Point
nodes.norm_label: data.ts is the single backend swap point

nodes.label: /portal/performance and /portal/feedback 404
nodes.rationale: Already linked from the sidebar but have no frame. Do not invent them.

nodes.label: Build Order: login, register, _shared, seam, roles
nodes.rationale: Login and register are built together because they share layout, background and form controls - doing them together is what puts those in the kit once instead of twice.
nodes.norm_label: build order: login, register, _shared, seam, roles

nodes.label: Register Has One Subfolder Per Role
nodes.rationale: Build one role's registration screen fully, extract its form chrome to the kit, then do the other three. The four almost certainly differ only in which fields they ask for; building all four inline leaves four copies of the same form to reconcile.
nodes.norm_label: register has one subfolder per role

nodes.label: How Does a Registrant Prove Role Entitlement?
nodes.rationale: Four separate sign-up forms means something has to stop a stranger opening the qac_admin one. Admin invite links, a domain-restricted email, or a pending-approval state are the usual answers - and it is a UI-visible decision, so ask before building the forms. The role must never be settable by the user at signup.
nodes.norm_label: how does a registrant prove role entitlement?

nodes.label: What URL Shape Do the Registration Screens Take?
nodes.rationale: /register/[role], four literal paths, or one /register with a role step - affects routing before any screen is built.
nodes.norm_label: what url shape do the registration screens take?

nodes.label: Schema-Shaped Questions to Ask as You Go
nodes.rationale: They cost nothing now and a UI assumption that contradicts the real model is a rebuild, not a rewire: dual roles, one accreditation per program or many cycles, rep scoping, and whether accreditors see only assigned accreditations.
nodes.norm_label: schema-shaped questions to ask as you go
nodes.community_name: Can One Person Hold Two Roles?

nodes.label: Per-Role Frame/Build Checklist
nodes.rationale: qac_personnel is 12 frames exported and 12 screens built, owner confirmation still open; login, register (five rows), _shared, program_representative, internal_accreditor and qac_admin are all unticked.
nodes.community_name: The Figma Export Is the Only Blocker Left in 3a

nodes.label: Portal Bold Is font-semibold
nodes.rationale: Except stat numerals and the Poppins wordmark, which are 700.

nodes.label: Phase 8 - Audit Log + Polish + Deploy (empty stub)
nodes.norm_label: phase 8 - audit log + polish + deploy (empty stub)
